records.name: Baker College of Clinton Township
records.campusFate: The Clinton Township campus was closed in 2020 and consolidated into Baker's new flagship campus in downtown Royal Oak; its 175,000 sq ft, 19-acre building at 34950 Little Mack Ave was put up for online auction on August 19, 2020.

evidence.claim: Clinton Township, Allen Park and Auburn Hills campuses will close and consolidate into a new Detroit-area campus, remaining open until August 2020.
Wikipedia states the Clinton Township and Allen Park campuses were closed with the move to the new campus in downtown Royal Oak.
Baker broke ground on an 86,000 sq ft flagship campus in Royal Oak in 2021, which opened in 2023.
Online auction of a 175,000 sq ft three-story school building on about 19 acres at 34950 Little Mack Ave, Clinton Township, on August 19, 2020; seller and result not stated, Baker not named.
Baker College Clinton Township Library is at 34950 Little Mack, Clinton Township, MI 48035, matching the auctioned address.

records.notes: Link between the auction listing and Baker rests on the matching address; the listing itself does not name Baker or the seller. Auction outcome and current owner not found. records.name: Baker College of Port Huron
records.campusFate: The Port Huron operation continues as part of Baker College, most visibly as the Culinary Institute of Michigan campus at 2000 St Clair St; what became of the former academic site at 3403 Lapeer Road was not established.

March 2022 Baker news item: CIM Port Huron received new ACFEF accreditation; CIM is presented as part of Baker College, with Port Huron one of Baker's campus options.
Baker's history page says Baker acquired Port Huron among other locations in 1990 and that Baker College of Port Huron opened a residence hall for culinary students in 2015.
Directory entry gives the old IPEDS-era address as 3403 Lapeer Road, Port Huron, and notes data unavailable since 2015 (status unconfirmed).

records.notes: The IPEDS fold into Baker College (UNITID 168847) appears to be a reporting consolidation: no page found describing the 2016 change. The culinary campus clearly continues under Baker College; the fate of the 3403 Lapeer Road academic site is unknown, and Wikipedia's current-campus list omits Port Huron. Could be coded not-a-closure as an administrative merger. Web search budget ran out before a final check of the Lapeer Road site.

records.name: Central Baptist Theological Seminary

evidence.claim: September 9, 2024 article quotes president Pam Durso saying the seminary has sold its 45,000 sq ft, largely unused building at 6601 Monticello Road, Shawnee, and will move in late December to under 9,000 sq ft at 8620 W. 110th Street, Overland Park; it has more than 450 students, mostly online. November 13, 2023 article: trustees approved selling the Shawnee campus under the plan 'The Future is Central' and the seminary will make virtual learning its primary model; school previously known as Central Baptist Theological Seminary.
Seminary website (copyright 2026) lists Central Seminary main campus at 8620 W. 110th Street, Suite 200, Overland Park, KS, with current programs and admissions.

records.notes: Buyer of the Shawnee building and the exact sale date were not found; sale reported as completed by 2024-09. The IPEDS exit in 2018 does not reflect a closure. centralseminary.edu is a different seminary (Plymouth, MN) and was not used as evidence for this institution.

records.name: Laura and Alvin Siegal College of Judaic Studies
records.campusFate: The college closed in 2012 when its adult-education work was folded into a Case Western Reserve University program; its final campus at 26500 Shaker Blvd., Beachwood, was a building it had shared since 1976 with the Agnon School, which continues there as the Joseph and Florence Mandel Jewish Day School.

evidence.claim: Encyclopedia of Cleveland History: in 2012 Siegal College and CWRU combined adult-education programs into the Siegal Lifelong Learning Program at CWRU and 'Siegal College closed under the new arrangement'; the college's final campus (from 1976) was 26500 Shaker Blvd., Beachwood; its library went to the Jewish Education Center of Cleveland. records.notes: The Siegal College page and the Mandel School page are separate; the shared-building link comes only from the Cleveland Jewish News chronology. Ownership of the building and any transfer date were not found, and the Agnon/Mandel school was a co-occupant since 1976, not a new buyer. The Mandel school is described as self-supporting and not affiliated with a congregation, so 'K-12 / charter' was used rather than 'Religious / mission'. Sources disagree on the rename year (2001 per CJN, 2002 per ECH). IPEDS last reported 2009; closure year 2012 rests on the ECH article. Whether the college left the building before 2012 is not stated. Merge note (audit): recoded from closed-campus-reused to closed-campus-unknown. The Mandel (Agnon) school shared the building from 1976 and is a co-occupant, not a buyer; no source on who owns or uses the building after the college closed.

records.buyerName: St. Joseph's Seminary and College (Dunwoodie, Yonkers), via the Diocese of Rockville Centre

evidence.claim: Seminary announced in Nov. 2011 it would stop training new priests as of Sept. 2012, merging the Rockville Centre program into St. Joseph's Seminary in Yonkers; as of Jan. 2024 it still offers theological courses as a satellite campus of St. Joseph Seminary and hosts Catholic retreats.

The Tablet (May 3, 2012): St. Joseph's Seminary becomes the degree-granting institution with Huntington as an extension site; Sacred Heart Institute for clergy formation to be headquartered there; building used for retreats and conferences.

records.notes: IPEDS 'dropped' in 2013 reflects the degree-granting authority moving to St. Joseph's, so this is administrative on the ground: the site was never closed. The campus is at 440 West Neck Road, Lloyd Harbor (Huntington mailing address). Search snippets (not fetched) mentioned a later plan, tied to the Diocese's bankruptcy, to sell about 200 of 216 acres to NY State Parks and the Village of Lloyd Harbor; this was not confirmed on a fetched page and is not reflected above. Closure date left null because the campus did not close; 2012 is when priestly formation ended.

records.name: Tennessee Temple University
records.campusFate: Tennessee Temple dissolved and merged into Piedmont International University (now Carolina University) in Winston-Salem, NC effective April 30, 2015, and its Chattanooga campus buildings were sold to Redemption to the Nations, a ministry that planned a Bible college there.
records.buyerName: Redemption to the Nations (parent organization of Redemption Point Church)

evidence.claim: March 3, 2015 report: the board voted to move and merge with Piedmont International University, merger to be finalized April 30, and the campus buildings were sold to Redemption to the Nations, which planned to open a Bible college there.

Announced it would dissolve and merge with Piedmont International University effective April 30, 2015; in February 2014 it announced it would sell most Highland Park campus buildings to Redemption to the Nations, parent of Redemption Point Church.
Tennessee Temple University dissolved and merged with Piedmont in 2015; Piedmont is now Carolina University; Temple Baptist Seminary name passed to Piedmont.

records.notes: Sale timing is inconsistent: Wikipedia says the sale was announced in Feb. 2014 for most buildings, and the Local3 article (March 2015) says the buildings were sold; no source gives a closing date, so transferDate is null. Current use of the Chattanooga campus was not verified (search budget exhausted); Redemption to the Nations may have changed plans. IPEDS exit year 2016 reflects data lag; the merger took effect in 2015. 'Educational reuse' reflects the buyer's stated plan for a Bible college, not a confirmed present use. Merge note (audit): confidence lowered from high. A March 2015 news report says the buildings were sold, but no closing date or current use was established.

records.name: American College of Traditional Chinese Medicine
records.campusFate: ACTCM became the fourth school of the California Institute of Integral Studies in 2015, CIIS decided in 2021 to close it, and it was to wind down in 2024 while seeking a subtenant for the leased San Francisco building it rented from the Archdiocese of San Francisco.

evidence.claim: August 2015 article: ACTCM's union with CIIS took effect July 1 and ACTCM became the fourth school of CIIS, creating the DACM degree.

ACTCM's parent CIIS decided in 2021 after an external audit to close it, with the college to 'cease to exist' in 2024; it rented a 12,000 sq ft building at 455 Arkansas St. from the Archdiocese of San Francisco under a lease to Sept. 30, 2024 and was seeking a subtenant.

records.notes: The input lists the combined-into institution as California Lutheran University (unitid 110413), but both fetched sources show the merger partner was the California Institute of Integral Studies in San Francisco; the input name looks mismatched. Closure year 2024 comes from a pre-closure article ('will close in 2024') and a UCSF finding aid snippet, so actual completion was not verified. The campus was leased, so there is no buyer; the post-lease use of the building is unknown. IPEDS exit year is 2016.

records.name: Antioch University Online
records.campusFate: Antioch University Online was a university-run online division with no campus of its own; its IPEDS unitid was folded into Antioch University's, with no change to a physical campus.

evidence.claim: An Antioch-hosted essay says AU Online grew out of a central university initiative (AU Virtual / AU Connected, c. 2013) to offer courses online nationally and 'existed until this most recent School reorganization in 2024-25'; it describes it as a university-level unit, not a separate institution.

records.notes: Outcome inferred from the page describing AUO as a central Antioch University initiative; the IPEDS 'combined' flag in 2021 is therefore read as administrative consolidation of reporting. No source fetched states the IPEDS merge directly. A web search summary also mentioned that Antioch University Midwest's programs were folded into AUO in 2020 when the Midwest building was put up for sale; that was not verified from a fetched page and concerns a different unitid. The essay's only reference to the 2024-25 reorganization gives no detail on what happened to AUO.

records.name: Goddard College
records.campusFate: Goddard announced closure in April 2024 and, after two earlier sale deals failed, trustees signed a purchase and sale agreement in October 2024 to sell the Plainfield campus to a New Hampshire redevelopment firm that said it intends to keep the historic buildings.

evidence.claim: Oct. 7, 2024: Goddard trustees entered a purchase and sale agreement with Execusuite LLC, a Lebanon, NH property redevelopment firm owned by Mike Davidson, who aims to maintain the existing structures; the college closed in spring 2024 citing declining enrollment and financial insolvency; closing date and price were not given.

Trustees signed a purchase and sales agreement with Mike Davidson of Execusuite; closing date not disclosed; Davidson does not plan to tear down the historic buildings; trustees announced the closure in April.

records.notes: Whether the Execusuite sale actually closed was not confirmed; searches found no 2025 coverage, and the Seven Days headline says 'has been sold' while its text describes only a signed agreement, so transferDate is left null. Two earlier deals (an unnamed buyer in May-July 2024 and the community nonprofit Greatwood Project in August-September 2024) collapsed. IPEDS gives a close date of 2024-08-02, which no fetched page confirms, so only the year is recorded. 'Speculative land' is a loose fit for a redevelopment firm with undisclosed plans. Merge note (audit): recoded from closed-campus-reused to closed-campus-unknown. Only a signed purchase and sale agreement (Oct 2024) is documented; no source confirms the sale closed.

records.name: Institute of Design and Construction
records.campusFate: The school sold its three-story Downtown Brooklyn building at 141 Willoughby Street in 2014 for $28 million to a developer, closed in July 2015, and the building was cleared in 2018-19 for a new mixed-use apartment tower.
records.buyerName: Savanna Partners (via 385 Gold Property Investors LLC)

evidence.claim: The Institute of Design and Construction voluntarily ceased operations in July 2015 due to declining enrollment and accreditation concerns from the New York State Board of Regents.

The school's property at 141 Willoughby Street was sold in 2014 for $28 million to 385 Gold Property Investors LLC, with developer Savanna Partners as new owner; a demolition permit issued in October 2018 and a 44-story, 203-apartment tower was planned.
A Dec. 31, 2014 article says the school occupied a three-story building at 141 Willoughby and that developer Savanna Partners planned a 30-story mixed-use tower to replace it.

records.notes: The school sold before it closed; it presumably operated under a sale arrangement until 2015 (not verified). Savanna is described in a search snippet (Goodwin Procter press release, not fetched) as a real estate private equity firm, which could justify 'Real estate capital' instead. The tower design changed between 2014 (30 stories), 2018 (44 stories) and a 2020 report (24 stories); a search snippet said the building was demolished in 2019, and whether the tower was built was not established. 'Speculative land' is a loose fit for a tower redevelopment.

records.name: Lambuth University
records.campusFate: After the Methodist-affiliated university closed in June 2011, the State of Tennessee, with local government and health-system partners funding the purchase, acquired the campus and the University of Memphis operates it as its Lambuth campus in Jackson.
records.buyerName: University of Memphis (Lambuth campus), acquired through the State of Tennessee with Jackson/Madison County local partners funding the $7.9 million purchase

evidence.claim: Dated Dec. 22, 2011: the University of Memphis officially took ownership of the former Lambuth campus after the deed was registered; local stakeholders paid about $2 million each toward the $7.9 million purchase; Lambuth closed June 30, 2011 after 168 years, was United Methodist-affiliated, and had been denied reaccreditation.

records.notes: Search results also indicated the University of Memphis began offering classes at the Lambuth campus in fall 2011, before formal deed transfer in December 2011, and that Lambuth had filed Chapter 11 in 2009; those details come from search summaries and were not confirmed on the fetched page. IPEDS status was 'dropped' but the institution did close.

records.name: Morthland College
records.campusFate: The college closed in 2018 after the U.S. Department of Education cut off federal student aid access; no fetched source says what happened to its West Frankfort buildings afterward.

evidence.claim: May 31, 2018 report that Morthland College announced its permanent closure for lack of funding after the Education Department blocked its access to federal student aid, which founder Tim Morthland disputes.
Morthland College closed in 2018 following a January 2017 federal and state investigation; the article lists several West Frankfort properties but gives no post-closure owner or use.

records.notes: Search summaries cited an Illinois Board of Higher Education statement of a July 31, 2018 closing date, but that PDF could not be fetched, so only the year is recorded. Search results mention a former Methodist church building donated to the college (leased back to the congregation for $1/20 years) and an Oak Street office building renovated with city TIF money; the fate of these after closure was not found. Described in sources as a Christian college; no denomination established.

records.name: Ohio College of Podiatric Medicine
records.campusFate: The college was acquired by Kent State University effective July 1, 2012 and continues as the Kent State University College of Podiatric Medicine at its existing Independence, Ohio site.

evidence.claim: Kent State news item posted July 9, 2012 stating the Ohio College of Podiatric Medicine officially became the Kent State University College of Podiatric Medicine effective July 1 and will remain at its current site at 6000 Rockside Woods Blvd., Independence, Ohio.

records.notes: The page states 'July 1' without a year; 2012 is inferred from the July 9, 2012 posting date and the IPEDS last year of 2012. The input lists city as blank; the college is in Independence, Ohio. Search results also described the Kent State trustees creating the college at a March 14 meeting and the OCPM board approving the acquisition.

records.name: St Tikhon's Orthodox Theological Seminary
records.campusFate: The seminary is still operating at its campus in South Canaan / Waymart, Pennsylvania, with accreditation renewed to 2034.

evidence.claim: Dated March 21, 2024 from South Canaan, PA: ATS reaffirmed St. Tikhon's Seminary's accreditation for ten years (to Spring 2034) and reaffirmed its M.Div. approval.
The seminary's own site, with a 2026 copyright line, lists its physical address as 178 Saint Tikhons Rd, Waymart, PA and mailing address in South Canaan, PA.

records.notes: IPEDS 'dropped' status after 2010 reflects the institution leaving the federal directory, not a closure; the likely reason (reclassification or ceasing Title IV participation) was not established.

records.name: Stevens-Henager College
records.campusFate: The Orem campus stopped instruction on Sept. 13, 2020, and the whole Stevens-Henager system closed in August 2021; no fetched source says what became of the Orem building.

evidence.claim: Four Stevens-Henager campuses, including Orem, Utah, were to stop instruction on Sept. 13, 2020; a vendor FAQ said no decisions had been made about the future of the physical campuses.
CEHE's colleges, including Stevens-Henager College, closed abruptly in August 2021 and all CEHE campuses were closed by early August 2021.

records.notes: Closure is well supported; campus afterlife is not. A search result surfaced a Coldwell Banker brochure offering the Stevens-Henager Utah portfolio (Orem, Ogden, Logan) as net-leased investment properties, which suggests the buildings were leased rather than owned by the college, but I did not open or date that document, so no buyer is recorded. Operator CEHE was a for-profit-run chain that had tried to convert to nonprofit status, which is why it appears in a nonprofit dataset.

records.notes: The 2021-08-01 date matches the IPEDS close date and a search-surfaced CEHE notice that all colleges would close as of August 1, 2021; the CEHE notice itself was not fetched.
